summary: Ajahn Khemadhammo works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Drama Centre London from around 1963 to 1966 and under Ajahn Chah as a traditional teacher from circa 1972 to 1977.
Ajahn Pasanno is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ajahn Chah from around 1975 to 1982. He served as founding co-abbot at Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery from circa 1996 to 2018.

Ajahn Sucitto specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a degree at the University of Warwick (circa 1968–1971), studied under Ajahn Sumedho in 1977, and served as abbot of Chithurst Buddhist Monastery from 1992 to 2014.

Ajahn Sumedho is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Washington, UC Berkeley (MA), and under Ajahn Chah. He founded and served as abbot of Wat Pa Nanachat (1975) and Amaravati Buddhist Monastery (1984–2010).
Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya is an Indologist who studied under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya. He held a position as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow at the University of Calcutta.

Akifumi Naito works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University, Honganji-ha Shōgakuin, and under Gadjin Nagao. He held posts at Ryukoku University (~1993), Shinshu Otaniha Institute, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

Akihiko Akamatsu specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University, Sorbonne Nouvelle/University of Paris, and under Yuichi Kajiyama. He held faculty posts at Kyushu University, Kyoto University, and Kyoto University's Hakubi Center.
Akihiro Oda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University. He held academic posts there as a lecturer (attested 1992) and later as Professor of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).
Akiko Kikuchi works in Buddhist studies. She was a research student at Minobusan University (attested 2026) and served as a professor at Musashino University (attested 2026).

Akiko Walley is a scholar of Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University and Harvard University, and held a position at the University of Oregon from 2009 to 2016.

Akimichi Eda specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Dr. phil. from the University of Marburg (attested 2005) under Michael Hahn, having also studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Khangkar Tsultrim Kelsang.
Akio Donohashi specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1967 to 1974 and served as a professor at Kobe University from 1990 to 1991.

Akio Minoura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Otani University as an associate professor (attested 2007–2013), Stanford University (2012–2013), and Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Akio Tanabe is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned degrees including a doctorate at the University of Tokyo and held academic positions at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, Kyoto University, and the University of Tokyo.
Akio Tatsuguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Ryukoku University, where he served as an assistant professor (attested 1987) and professor emeritus (attested 2015).

Akira Fujieda specialized in Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University (~1931–1934), he worked at the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kyoto University (professor in 1968), and held visiting professorships at Copenhagen and UC Berkeley.
Akira Hataya is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held an assistant professorship at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and is an emeritus professor at Otani University (attested 2014).

Akira Hirakawa specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Shoson Miyamoto, later becoming a professor there (1962–1975). He also held posts at Waseda University and the ICPBS.

Akira Miyaji specializes in Buddhist studies, archaeology, and Indology. Educated through his doctorate at Nagoya University, he held posts at Hirosaki University, Nagoya University, Shizuoka Prefectural Museum of Art, and Ryukoku University and Museum.

Akira Mukai is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Hokkaido University (~1969–1975). He served as an assistant at Hokkaido University (~1975) and professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).
